title: Find out whether a long edit goes quiet after its first 48 pieces of sound
goal: Playing the 20 minute reference edit, the sound engine said it left out 95 pieces of sound because more were alive than it schedules at once. If nothing schedules them later, a person playing a long edit from the start hears the sound stop part way through while the picture goes on. Find out whether that is what happens, and if it is, make every piece play when its time comes.
notes: Seen by the speed walk (task a-speed-walk-measures-the-long-reference-edit-th), 2026-11-13 00:14: Scripts/perf/speed-walk.sh --long 20 printed for the play step: "sound: 95 piece(s) left out, silent at 0 of 2 one-second looks" (DocumentAudioPlayer.droppedSegments). The 6 minute edit reads 0 left out. Code read, not yet heard: DocumentAudioPlayer.play keeps live.prefix(segmentBudget = 48) sorted by start and nothing reschedules later pieces (followAudio -> follow only sets levels). The silent-look count is not evidence either way: the main thread let the walk look only twice in a minute. Unconfirmed by ear, hence p2.
acceptance: Play the 20 minute reference edit from the start at Next defaults and say, with a measurement of what the engine has scheduled at each minute, whether any clip's sound or the music is missing after the first few minutes
If sound goes missing, every piece of sound in the 20 and 60 minute edits plays at its moment, measured the same way
The speed walk's sound numbers (pieces left out, silent looks) read zero on the 20 minute edit

log.note: Measured (scratch core test over ReferenceEdit.build + audioMix, then what play() keeps = first 48 by start): 20 min edit has 144 audible pieces, at most 3 alive at any moment; played from 0 the engine holds pieces only up to 385 s. Per minute (audible at mm:30 / on the engine): 0-5 all present, 6: 2/1, 7-19: 2/0. 60 min edit: 431 pieces, last scheduled ends 380 s, minutes 7-59 have 0 on the engine. So yes: from the start, all sound stops at about 6:25 and never comes back. The 'more alive than the budget' comment is wrong: play() counts every piece still to come, not those alive at once. Adversarial: fix must not depend on the main thread (it stalled for seconds on long edits), so the top-up runs on the engine's own queue off the audio clock; late nodes must land in step with nodes scheduled at the press, so their delay is read off a silent clock node that has played since the press.

Reproduced in the probe on today's engine (shim exposing what play() scheduled): Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/perf/walks/long-20-sound.json, 20 min edit played from 0:00 for 450 s: 'sound: 96 piece(s) left out, silent at 66 of 450 one-second looks (first at 6:24.9), level heard at each minute 0:0.036 1:0.031 2:0.022 3:0.035 4:0.045 5:0.039 6:0.033 7:0.018'. Minute 7's 0.018 is the music alone: one 78 s music piece from 5:48 to 7:06 was among the 48; every voice was gone from 6:25 and the music too from 7:06.

Fixed: the engine holds only what starts within 20 s of the playhead (AudioScheduleWindow, PhotonzCore, 9 tests incl. both reference edits simulated whole), tops it up every 0.5 s on its own queue off a silent clock node, gives back finished nodes and idle layer mixers; budget is now 48 at once. Late pieces start at an exact host time (first try anchored at the next render landed 43 ms off; host-time anchoring reads 1 ms). After, same walk: 20 min 'sound: 0 piece(s) left out, silent at 0 of 450 one-second looks, level heard at each minute 0:0.037 1:0.031 2:0.030 3:0.040 4:0.041 5:0.039 6:0.032 7:0.034'; 60 min (long-60-sound.json) '0 left out, silent at 0 of 450, 0:0.034 ... 6:0.023 7:0.042, late pieces within 1ms'. Short speed walk: 32 numbers within baseline, sound 0/0 of 60. Acceptance 3 is read off long-20-sound.json, which is the speed walk's own play measure on the 20 min edit from 0:00 for 450 s; the full long-20 speed walk (play from 0:15 for 60 s, inside the old 48 anyway) was not re-run. Also fixed in passing: a playthrough whose first sound is more than 20 s after the press still starts its clock (test aSoundLongAfterThePressIsPutOnWhenItComesUp). soundExpectPlaying now checks every piece sounding at the playhead is on the engine. Walks: 8 of 9 sound/speed walks ok first time, playback-speed-on-the-reference-edit-walk failed once on picture lag (4 frames behind at one look) and passed on re-run, not sound related, left in this log. Filed find-out-whether-the-sound-plays-a-fifth-of-a-se (engine clock ~183 ms behind the playhead at the median, unconfirmed against the shown picture, p2). Audit: queue/audits/2026-11-17-long-edit-sound-plays-to-the-end.json.

Yes, it went quiet: played from 0:00 the 20 and 60 min edits lost every voice at 6:24.9 (66 of 450 looks silent). Fixed in DocumentAudioPlayer with a rolling 20 s window (AudioScheduleWindow, PhotonzCore, tested over both edits whole) topped up off the engine's own clock. Measured after with Scripts/perf/walks/long-20-sound.json and long-60-sound.json: 0 left out, 0 of 450 silent, voice level every minute, late pieces within 1 ms. Suite green, 9 sound/speed walks ok, short speed walk inside its baseline. Audit queue/audits/2026-11-17-long-edit-sound-plays-to-the-end.json.
